title: The pull request loop, without a website
summary: Branch, push, review, address feedback, merge, delete. Run the whole GitHub flow against a real bare repository so you can see exactly which git commands the buttons on a website are pressing for you.
mental_model: A pull request is not a git concept. It is a website's name for 'the diff between this branch and its merge base, plus a comment thread'. Every button on it maps to a command you can run yourself.

steps.title: Branch from an up-to-date main
steps.why: Fetch first, branch from `origin/main` rather than your possibly-stale local main. Skipping this is the most common cause of a pull request that shows unrelated commits.

verify.label: you are on a feature branch from origin/main

steps.title: Make the change in reviewable commits
steps.why: Two commits, each doing one thing. A reviewer can read them in order and understand the shape of the change before reading a single line of the diff.

write.content:
PH_LOW = 7.8
PH_HIGH = 8.4


def check_ph(value):
    return PH_LOW <= value <= PH_HIGH

from alerts import check_ph

print('reef controller')
print(check_ph(8.1))

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Wire the pH check into the entrypoint"

steps.title: Publish it — this is 'open a pull request'
steps.why: Pushing the branch is the whole mechanical act. The website adds a title, a description and a place to argue; git adds nothing further.

verify.label: the branch is published for review

steps.title: See exactly what a reviewer sees
steps.why: Three dots, not two. A pull request shows `origin/main...HEAD` — your changes since the fork point, without main's own later commits mixed in.

steps.title: The reviewer looks at it in their own clone
steps.why: Anyone can check out a published branch and run it. This is what a reviewer should do before approving anything non-trivial — reading a diff in a browser is not the same as running the code.
steps.expect: The branch, checked out and runnable, in a second working copy.

steps.title: Address the review comment
steps.why: The reviewer wants the boundary values documented. Amend or add a commit — either is fine, but if the branch is pushed you must force, and `--force-with-lease` is the safe spelling.

write.content:
# Safe range for a mixed reef tank; outside this, corals bleach.
PH_LOW = 7.8
PH_HIGH = 8.4


def check_ph(value):
    """True when the reading is inside the safe range, inclusive."""
    return PH_LOW <= value <= PH_HIGH

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Document the pH safe range"

steps.expect: A third commit, pushed as a fast-forward — reviewers can see what changed since their comment.

verify.label: the review response is a visible extra commit

steps.title: Merge it — the green button
steps.why: `--no-ff` records that a branch existed and which commits it contained. That is what the 'Create a merge commit' option does; 'Squash and merge' would be `--squash` instead.
commands: git merge --no-ff -m "Merge pull request: pH alerts" feature/ph-alerts

verify.label: the feature is on main, on the server

steps.title: Delete the branch, both copies
steps.why: The last button on the page. Two deletions, because local and remote branches are separate things — and a repository nobody cleans up becomes unnavigable within a quarter.

verify.label: the branch is gone locally and remotely
verify.hint: git push origin --delete, then git branch -d

verify.label: the whole feature, including the review response, is on main
it landed as a merge commit, so the branch is visible in history
the branch was cleaned up afterwards

pitfalls: Branch from `origin/main` after a fetch, not from a local main you last updated on Tuesday.
Force-pushing a branch under review invalidates the reviewer's place in the diff. Prefer extra commits during review, and squash at merge time if you want a clean history.
The pull-request diff is the three-dot diff. If it shows changes you did not make, your branch needs rebasing or you are reading a two-dot diff.
Deleting the remote branch does not delete your local one. Both, every time, or `git branch -a` becomes useless.
cheatsheet: branch from the server's current state
push review responses as extra commits
